conventions.convention: Velocity tests lie in the real space V=H¹₀(D)ᵈ; pressure uses Q=L²₀(D), b(v,p)=−(p,div v), and aν(u,v)=2ν(ε(u),ε(v)).
The convective form is one half of the advective pairing minus its last-slot transpose. Its energy cancellation does not require exact discrete divergence freedom.
Hσ is the L² closure of Vσ, whereas Z_h is the weak MINI divergence kernel; Z_h is not identified with the pointwise divergence-free space.
A pressure-bearing energy weak solution requires p∈L⁴ᐟ³(0,T;Q). A solenoidal energy weak velocity imposes no such pressure requirement.

Time steps are arbitrary positive partition lengths; forcing is averaged by Bochner integration over each cell. The convergence and smooth-error statements use the L²-orthogonal mass initialization P_Zh u₀.
Pressure primitives start at zero and are interpolated continuously and affinely between time nodes; their derivatives are the right-constant reconstructed pressures.
The smooth velocity estimate requires τmaxΛ≤1/2 and retains exponential dependence on Λ=1+C_Dν⁻³M_u⁴; it is not viscosity-uniform.
The Taylor–Green example uses periodic identification of opposite edges of (0,2π)² and is separate from the no-slip bounded-domain branch.
The graded-mesh counterexample fixes its finite geometric template and shape bound before varying recursive depth; its global maximum mesh diameter need not tend to zero.

load_bearing.statement: The skew form is continuous on V³, cancels in its last two equal slots, and satisfies |c(a;b,w)|≤C_D‖a‖₂¹ᐟ²‖∇a‖₂¹ᐟ²‖∇b‖₂‖∇w‖₂. Energy velocities give convection in L⁴ᐟ³(0,T;V*); exactly solenoidal two-dimensional velocities admit the sharper stated bound.

Under Countable Choice, every finite positive time partition and initial u_h⁰∈Z_h admit a mixed backward Euler MINI solution. Every solution satisfies the displayed work-form energy inequality and its mesh-independent forcing bound.
The constructed MINI Fortin map satisfies ‖v−Π_hv‖₂≤Ch‖∇v‖₂, converges strongly in H¹₀ for each fixed v as h→0, and maps Vσ into Z_h.

Under the stated uniform energy bounds, vanishing mesh and maximum time-step sizes, and finite solenoidal coefficient difference bounds in L⁴ᐟ³, the weakly solenoidal MINI reconstructions are relatively compact in L²(0,T;L²(D)ᵈ).

For the stated shape-regular meshes and independently vanishing maximum time steps, mass-initialized MINI solutions have a subsequence converging strongly in L²_tL²_x and weakly in L²_tH¹₀ to a solenoidal energy weak velocity.

Every stated solenoidal energy weak velocity has a unique bounded weakly continuous mean-zero pressure primitive P with P(0)=0. The discrete primitives obey the displayed uniform bound and converge weakly along a further subsequence, yielding weak pressure convergence as time distributions. Regular L⁴ᐟ³_tQ pressure exists if and only if the actual full derivative belongs to L⁴ᐟ³_tV*.
Under the Axiom of Choice, the stated two-dimensional solenoidal energy weak velocities are unique, strongly continuous into Hσ, belong to L⁴_tL⁴_x, and have actual restricted derivative in L²_tVσ*.

Under the stated smooth no-slip branch assumptions, mass initialization, and τmaxΛ≤1/2, any backward Euler MINI solution satisfies the displayed nodal L² plus accumulated V-norm velocity error bound C_*(hM+τmaxM²).

For the stated logarithmic initial profile with 1/2<α≤3/4, the halfline Dirichlet heat mass derivative satisfies −m′(t) comparable to t⁻³ᐟ⁴(log(1/t))⁻α near zero; m′ is integrable but not L⁴ᐟ³, while the displayed squared corrector expression is integrable.
